text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where team members integrate their code changes frequently, often several times a day. The core of CI is the automated build process, which compiles the code every time a change is pushed. Along with building, the system also runs a series of automated tests. These tests check for bugs, logic errors, and performance problems. The main advantage is catching issues early. If a test fails, the team knows immediately and can fix the problem before it grows larger. CI pipelines handle this entire workflow automatically, from code commit to test results, saving time and reducing manual errors.
